# A pure js:// function returning a TS enum member folds to that member.
#
# At runtime the member is erased to its value — 1 for a numeric enum, "warn"
# for a string one — so the encoder writes a bare number or string with nothing
# on it naming the enum it came from. The declared return type is the only
# thing that says which enum, and the member is the one whose declared value
# equals the literal.
#
# The member goes back out the same way it came in: what the page carries is
# the value the declaration gives it, not the SNGL member name, because the
# value is what the module's own code compares against — `Color.Green` in
# index.js is 1, and a page holding "Green" would agree with nothing.
#
# The enum lives in a .d.ts beside its .js, which is how a compiled package
# ships one and also the only shape node can run: node executes TypeScript by
# stripping types, and an enum is not a type — it emits an object.
[!node] skip
env SNGL_CONSTEVAL_CACHE=$WORK/evalcache

sngl generate --lang=none --platform=html --out=out app.sngl
exists out/index.html

# The value is what proves the right member was picked: 1 could only have come
# back as Green, and "warn" as Warn.
grep 'var c = 1' out/index.html
grep 'var l = "warn"' out/index.html
! grep '"Green"' out/index.html
! grep 'pickColor' out/index.html
! grep 'pickLevel' out/index.html

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl://std"
import lib "js://./lib"

const c = lib.pickColor()
const l = lib.pickLevel()

component main {
    if c == lib.Color.Green {
        text(value="green wins")
    }
    if l == lib.Level.Warn {
        text(value="warn wins")
    }
}
-- lib/index.d.ts --
export declare enum Color {
    Red = 0,
    Green = 1,
    Blue = 2,
}

export declare enum Level {
    Info = "info",
    Warn = "warn",
}

/** @sngl-pure */
export declare function pickColor(): Color;

/** @sngl-pure */
export declare function pickLevel(): Level;

-- lib/index.js --
export const Color = { 0: "Red", Red: 0, 1: "Green", Green: 1, 2: "Blue", Blue: 2 };
export const Level = { Info: "info", Warn: "warn" };

export function pickColor() {
    return Color.Green;
}

export function pickLevel() {
    return Level.Warn;
}
